title: Matter — Material Affordance Chain
subtitle: Pressure, folding, wetting, and surface memory across materials
lineage: Lineage: Provisional Operator SCION 061 · Material Affordance Chain
theorem: Make one material behavior lead to another through observable transformation: pressure, folding, wetting, adhesion, or release. Treat resemblance as a way to discover what materials can do.
boundary_note: The cut from wetted paper to dry soil/eroded rock is explicitly labeled as a visual analogy rather than a time-lapse of the same object.

v1_defect_timecodes: Seg #06 (t=25.30s-30.80s) & Seg #08 Quad BR: `096cef84` shows people walking among vineyard grapevines with an internal cut instead of a close-up weathered surface.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: Seg #06, labeled as a close view of a 'cracked, weathered surface', actually shows people walking through a vineyard in wide/medium shots.
critic_tribunal.causal_hypothesis: OpenCLIP metadata false positive on `The Soil Explorers` matching 'soil/weathered' to an outdoor vineyard walk.
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Replace Seg #06 and the 4th Quad panel with verified close-up tactile soil/eroded rock shots `8b6296d7` (`0.05s-3.25s`, hand pressing directly into dry soil) and `5e0c2fa9` (`9.50s-15.00s`, exposed eroded rock/soil face).
critic_tribunal.strength_to_preserve: The tactile tabletop chain across `3afead43` (`The Photographer`, 1948), `159c6a16` (`All My Babies`, 1953), `05d0d040`, and `e1401c9e` (`From Dreams to Reality`).
